summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR20.3 billion and EBITDA margin hit 27.1%, the top of the mid-20s guidance band, with net zero debt.
summary.overview: GE Vernova T&D India reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR20.3 billion, up 32% YoY, with H1 revenue of INR38.6 billion, up 35%. Q2 order intake was INR24.4 billion, up 52% YoY, taking H1 intake to about INR35.8 billion (up 11%), and order backlog ended at INR214.4 billion. EBITDA was INR5.5 billion (27.1% of revenue) and PAT was INR4.3 billion (21.3%), with cash and equivalents of about INR32.5 billion. Management reiterated mid-20s EBITDA guidance for the full year and said HVDC execution will mostly start from FY28, while two related-party export orders are on hold or pending.

segments.name: Transmission equipment (single segment)
segments.commentary: Company reports one segment (high-voltage transmission products), so no split for software and services; management said that share may have dropped as equipment orders grew faster.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export share was 21% of Q2 orders and 32% of Q2 revenue; H1 export share was 29% of orders and 31% of revenue. Management says export orders carry higher margin than domestic, by about 500 bps as previously indicated.

guidance_outlook: Mid-20s EBITDA margin guidance maintained for FY27; H1 EBITDA was about 26.2%.
No significant HVDC execution revenue expected in FY27 or the next financial year; significant HVDC contribution expected from FY28.
Management does not give gross margin guidance and does not share long-range guidance; FY27 base order expectation of INR70-80 billion was kept unchanged.
Expects revenue growth of more than 30% a year over the next three years, supported by backlog plus HVDC L1 position, with about INR10 billion capacity expansion.
Expects at least 2-3 HVDC projects to come in the next year; a sizable STATCOM order is expected in Q4.
Expects data-center traction to strengthen from Q4 or next year; India data-center share of backlog is less than 2%.
risks_watch: Two related-party export orders (about INR31 billion lapsed; US $151 million approval valid to 15 May 2027) depend on customer timing and are not in backlog.
Supply-chain risk: management called it the top operational risk; 765 kV bushings are mostly imported with lead times above 15-18 months.
Revenue mix shifting toward equipment and away from services; no segment disclosure for software and services.
Pricing pressure on regular high-voltage transformers, while copper prices have risen sharply.
Timing of HVDC execution (mostly FY28 onward) and its margin profile, which management has not guided.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on order flow, margins and execution, but guarded on forward specifics: management declined gross margin and long-range guidance, and gave vague timing on the held related-party orders, Trench synergies and competition.
key_quotes: We are confident of converting our INR214 billion backlog profitably over the coming years.
So, for the entire year, Aditya, we will maintain our guidance of mid-20s EBITDA margin.
We don't give gross margin guidance. We have given EBITDA guidance.
There was no one-offs. It was all regular orders which have come in.

qa_highlights.question: Will the parent's Trench acquisition and planned Trench manufacturing in India be part of GE Vernova T&D India, and what is the services and software revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to comment on Trench as the deal closes later in FY27. It does not disclose services and software revenue because it reports one segment; the share may have dropped as equipment orders grew faster.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 2 related-party export orders on hold likely to clear in 6-12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: The customer put the hold on due to bigger project size and it is unclear whether it lifts in 6, 8 or 12 months, so too early to speculate. The US related-party order is in discussion, with a hope to conclude in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin be sustained at the high level for the next two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the company will maintain mid-20s EBITDA margin guidance for the full year. Management declined to guide on gross margin, which it said varies quarter to quarter by mix, and H1 EBITDA was about 26.2%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Barmer HVDC order hurt EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution is expected over the next 2-4 financial years, with no significant HVDC execution revenue in FY27 and no significant contribution next year; significant HVDC revenue starts from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is any part of the backlog cancelled due to data-centre issues, and what is the sensed market risk?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said there is no sense of any cancellation and that he was not aware of such queries. India data-centre share of backlog is less than 2%.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin outlook once HVDC execution starts, given competition?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO clarified gross margin is around 45% in Q2, not 55%-57%. He declined to give gross margin guidance, citing operating leverage and mix, and said long-range guidance will be communicated later.

capex_capacity: Capacity expansion programme of about INR10 billion (also referred to as INR1,100 crore capex); roughly 20% already incurred as of the call.
Management says more than 90% of the investment is in existing plants where land is already held, giving integrated expansion with lower capex need than peers for similar volume.
Utilisation at most factories described as pretty high; asked whether above 75%, CEO answered yes.
Localisation: HVDC transformers, thyristor valves and controls now manufactured in India; sub-vendor components such as CRGO and oil still imported; localisation to be taken component by component.
765 kV bushings mostly imported; domestic capacity limited but expansion under way; 765 kV bushing lead times more than 15-18 months, transformer build 3-4 months.
Asia has two transformer factories per management: Indonesia (up to 245 kV) and Vadodara (higher ratings).

Commissioned in Q2: 400 kV substation for NEA Nepal, 400 kV GIS at Babarzar (GETCO), 765 kV reactors for PGCIL at Bidar and Resonia at Beawar, 765 kV generator transformer for NUPPL at Ghatampur, GIS at Narela Delhi, export jobs in Spain and Senegal.
demand_pricing: Q2 order intake INR24.4 billion (+52% YoY vs INR16.1 billion); H1 order intake about INR35.8 billion (+11%); backlog INR214.4 billion at Sept 2026 vs INR214.6 billion at March 2026, said to be more than 3 years of revenue.

Key Q2 wins: 400 kV generator transformer and 420 kV GIS for a 1,500 MW pumped storage project in Maharashtra; 800 kV and 420 kV GIS for Andhra Pradesh transmission; 400 kV reactors and 420/220 kV GIS for a TBCB project in Himachal Pradesh; 765 kV shunt reactor for a TBCB project in Andhra Pradesh.
Export share: 21% of Q2 orders and 32% of Q2 revenue; H1 29% of orders and 31% of revenue. H1 export orders INR10.4 billion, largely related-party, vs INR11.8 billion in full FY26.

Two related-party export approvals: about INR31 billion for HV switchgear components to Middle East and France customers lapsed at 2026 AGM (customer hold); US entity approval for about $151 million valid to 15 May 2027, order in discussion, hoped to conclude in H2 FY27. Neither is in backlog.
Domestic pipeline: lowest bidder for Power Grid Barmer HVDC (awarded to Power Grid); strong TBCB pipeline over last 3-4 months; management expects strong pipeline for next 4-5 months.

Pricing: slight pressure on regular high-voltage transformer prices, described as very little; no HVDC tender since Barmer, so no competitive-intensity read on HVDC. Management did not see the copper-driven pricing uplift that an analyst expected.
Export orders carry higher margin than domestic, about 500 bps, trend unchanged per management.
Data centres: India data-centre installed base about 1.5 GW, expected 8-10 GW by 2030; India data-centre share of backlog less than 2%; stronger traction expected from Q4 or next year.
Trench acquisition by parent (announced about two days before the call) expected to close in later part of FY27; management said too early to comment on India integration.

adds.what: Capacity expansion programme of about INR10 billion (INR1,100 crore) at existing plants, ~20% incurred

growth.why: Management maintained mid-20s FY27 EBITDA margin and base domestic orders of INR70-80bn, and expects revenue growth above 30% a year for three years backed by INR214bn backlog, HVDC L1 position and a ~INR10bn capacity expansion (about 20% spent), though HVDC revenue only starts in FY28 and two related-party export orders (~INR31bn and ~$151m) are on hold or pending.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management maintained mid-20s full-year EBITDA guidance with H1 at about 26.2% and Q2 at 27.1%, while Q2 gross margin was about 45% and export orders carry about 500 bps higher margin; gross margin guidance was declined.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About INR10 billion (INR1,100 crore) capacity expansion at existing plants is under way with about 20% already incurred, and the company says more than 90% sits on land already held.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue rose 32% YoY to INR20.3 billion and H1 revenue 35% to INR38.6 billion, with INR214.4 billion backlog (more than 3 years of revenue) and management expecting above 30% revenue growth a year for three years.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is described as pretty high at most factories (CEO said above 75%), and the INR10 billion expansion is already under way, so a further capex step is plausible though not guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only maintained mid-20s EBITDA margin and base domestic orders of INR70-80 billion, and did not raise guidance even with Q2 revenue up 32% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Top operational risk is supply chain, with 765 kV bushing lead times above 15-18 months, and pricing pressure on regular HV transformers, though management has not signalled a cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: HVDC execution starts mostly in FY28 with 2-3 HVDC projects expected in the next year, but no specific new product launch was named.

rows.label: Related-party export orders (INR31bn lapsed, US$151m approval)
rows.why: The US entity approval for about $151 million (valid to 15 May 2027) is in discussion and hoped to conclude in H2 FY27, but the INR31 billion lapsed order is on customer hold and not in backlog.

rows.label: STATCOM and HVDC order flow
rows.why: Management expects at least 2-3 HVDC projects in the next year and a sizable STATCOM order in Q4, against an HVDC L1 position on Barmer that has been awarded to Power Grid.

rows.label: Data-centre traction
rows.why: India data-centre share of backlog is under 2% against an installed base of about 1.5 GW and an expected 8-10 GW by 2030, with traction expected from Q4 or next year.

tone.note: Management was confident on order flow, the 27.1% Q2 EBITDA margin and the INR10 billion capacity expansion, but guarded on gross margin, HVDC timing, held related-party orders and Trench synergies; analysts pressed on margin sustainability, HVDC margin dilution and backlog cancellation risk.
